title: Master Engineering Coordinator — System Overview
description: One objective in; four systems delegated; one honest report out. The master runs the pipeline for real.
body: The Master AI Engineering Coordinator is the conductor of the five-system build. Given an engineering objective in plain words, it extracts keywords, asks the knowledge coordinator for relevant databases, asks the tool registry for matching capabilities, hands a matched build pattern to the generator, and sends the result to the verification lab — then reports what worked at every stage with earned verification statuses. The demonstration runs the full pipeline on "build a temperature converter": all four stages tested, artifact generated and verified. It is a deterministic orchestrator, not a general intelligence, and its limits are documented, not hidden.

demo.program: node master-engineering-coordinator.js run build a temperature converter

title: Honest Refusal — "build a warp drive"
description: Objectives outside the capability map are reported as proposed — never built, never faked.
body: This record is the honesty guarantee. The demonstration runs the master on "build a warp drive": no pattern matches, nothing is generated, and the report states plainly that the objective is proposed and unbuilt, with a note explaining why. A coordinator that cannot say "I can't build that" cannot be trusted when it says it can.

title: Limits — Deterministic Orchestrator, Not General Intelligence
t: Limits — Deterministic Orchestrator, Not General Intelligence
description: The master matches patterns; it does not reason, learn, or invent new engineering approaches.
body: The most important record in this database. The master coordinator is a deterministic pipeline: keyword extraction, manifest search, registry lookup, pattern-matched generation, lab verification. It cannot design a fusion reactor, write novel algorithms, or improve itself. Calling it "AI" refers to its role as the coordinating intelligence of this five-system build, not to general intelligence — and the demonstration proves the boundary by showing an unmatched objective reported as proposed.

title: Verification-Status Vocabulary — What Each Word Means
t: Verification-Status Vocabulary — What Each Word Means
description: proposed, generated, executable, tested, independently-verified: each earned only by its gate.
body: The vocabulary is the contract. proposed: described but not built. generated: files exist. executable: runs with exit 0. tested: declared tests pass. independently-verified: confirmed by a party other than the builder — a status none of these systems claim yet, because no independent party has verified them. The demonstration prints the vocabulary with the gate each word requires.
